Or because they belittled the believers and called them "the lowest" (arādhil), from his words: ﴿Let no one among us be ignorant﴾. Or: ﴿you are ignorant﴾ of the meeting with your Lord; or: you are ignorant that they are better than you; or: their description as ignorant refers to this proposal, which is driving away the believers and the like.

﴿who will help me﴾ is an interrogative whose meaning is: there is no helper for me against God's punishment if I drive them away from the good which they have accepted, or because of their faith. This was said by al-Farra'. They used to ask him to drive them away so that they would believe in him, out of pride, not wanting to be on an equal footing with them. Then he made them stand (before the question) with his words: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ [Yunus: 3], to consider the reasoning which leads to the soundness of this argument. The explanation of the three sentences has already been given in al-Anʿam.

tazdarī: it is of the form tafʿalī (ifta'ala pattern), and the dāl is a substitute for the tā'. He said: "You see the slender man and you despise him, while in his garments there is a lion, fierce." And al-Farra' quoted: "The friend keeps away from him, and his wife despises him, and the young child rebukes him." The returning pronoun to the relative is deleted, i.e. tazdarūnahum (you despise them), i.e. your eyes look down on them. The object of "will not give them" (lan yu'tiyahum) is the complement of his words "and I do not say" (wa lā aqūlu). And "for those who" (lillādhīna) means "for the sake of those who". Had the lām been for conveying (the message), the grammatical form would have been "will not give you" (lan yu'tiyakum) with the kāf of address; i.e. your contempt for them does not diminish their reward before God, nor does it nullify their wages.

﴿God knows best what is in their souls﴾: a submission to God, i.e. I do not judge them by anything of this; the judgment in that belongs to God, the Exalted, who knows what is in their souls and will recompense them for it.

It was said: this is a reply to their words: "Only the lowest of us have followed you," i.e. I do not judge them as having no good because of your suspicion about them; indeed their inner states are not like their outward appearances; God, Mighty and Majestic, knows best what is in their souls. ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾: if I did that, I would be among the wrongdoers, who put things in other than their proper places.

﴿You have disputed with us﴾: the apparent meaning is exaggeration in contention and argument. al-Kalbi said: "You have called us (to God)." It was said: "You have admonished us." It was said: "You brought all kinds of disputation and its varieties, so your claim is not established." Ibn ʿAbbas read: fa-akthharta jadalanā (you have multiplied our disputation), like His words: ﴿And man is most of all things contentious﴾ [al-Kahf: 54]. ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with﴾: the hastened punishment. The mā (what) means "that which" with a deleted returning pronoun, i.e. what you threaten us with, or it is a verbal-noun (maṣdariyya) particle, i.e. your threat.

The reason his disputing with them was so frequent is that he remained among them for what God had informed about: a thousand years less fifty years. And at every time he called them to God, and they answered him by worshipping their idols.

He said: ﴿It is only God who will bring it to you﴾, i.e. that is not up to me; it belongs only to the God who will punish you for your disobedience. ﴿If He wills﴾, i.e. if His wisdom requires that He hasten your punishment while you are in His grasp, you cannot escape from Him, nor can you resist Him.

When they said: ﴿You have disputed with us﴾, and asked for the punishment to be hastened, and his disputing with them was only for the sake of counsel and rescue from God's punishment, he said: ﴿My counsel will not benefit you﴾. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafī read nuṣḥī (my counsel) with a fatḥa on the nūn, and it is a verbal noun (maṣdar).

The reading of the majority is with a ḍamma on it (nuṣḥī). It is possible that it is a verbal noun, like shukr (thanks), and possible that it is a noun (ism). These two conditions: the first of them is linked to His words ﴿my counsel will not benefit you﴾, and this is evidence of the answer to the condition; its estimated form: "If I wish to advise you, then my counsel will not benefit you." The second condition is linked to the first condition, and its answer is also what His words ﴿my counsel will not benefit you﴾ indicate; its estimated form: "If God wishes to lead you astray, then my counsel will not benefit you." The second condition became a condition within the first; the earlier became later and the later became earlier. As if the structure were: "If I wish to advise you, if God wishes to lead you astray, then my counsel will not benefit you." In meaning it is like a conditional with fa (then), e.g.: "If God wishes to lead you astray, then if I wish to advise you, my counsel will not benefit you." A parallel to this is: ﴿and a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50].

al-Zamakhshari said: His words ﴿if God wishes to lead you astray﴾ have as their answer what His words ﴿my counsel will not benefit you﴾ indicate; this indication has the force of what it indicates, so it is connected by a condition, just as the answer is connected to the condition in the saying: "If you do good to me, I will do good to you, if I am able." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "My counsel to you does not benefit, nor does my wish for your good suffice, if God, the Exalted, has willed for you misguidance, perdition and destruction."

The second condition is an interjection within the speech, and in it there is eloquence from the combination of the two wills, and that the will of humans is not sufficient. The connection of this condition is to "my counsel", and the connection of the other is to "will not benefit". End. Likewise Abu al-Faraj Ibn al-Jawzi said: the answer of the first is "the counsel", and the answer of the second is "the benefit."

The apparent meaning of yughwiyakum (lead you astray) is yuḍillakum (lead you into error), from the saying: ghawā al-rajul yaghwī (the man went astray), which means misguidance. In it the attribution of misguidance to God is present, so it is an argument against the Mu'tazilites, who say that misguidance comes from the servant. al-Zamakhshari said: when God knows that the unbeliever is persistent, He leaves him to his own affairs and does not compel him; that is called ghiwāya (misguidance) and imlā' (respite). Just as when He knows from him that he will repent and turn back, He shows him kindness, and that is called irshād (guidance) and hidāya (right guidance). End.

This is in the manner of the Mu'tazila, and they stated that God is not described as "knowing" (ʿārif), so one should not say "when God knows", as al-Zamakhshari said. The Mu'tazilite may say: it is not necessary that in (in idhā... ) the particle in be conditional; rather it is negative, and the meaning is: God did not wish to lead you astray. In that there is evidence for negating misguidance from God, Exalted. And His words ﴿my counsel will not benefit you if I wish to advise you﴾ would be information from him to them and a consolation to himself regarding them, because of what he saw of their persistence and their continuing in disbelief.

It was said: the meaning of (yughwiyakum) is: yuhlikakum (destroy you), and al-ghawā means illness and perdition. In the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ: "So-and-so became ghāwiyan" meaning sick. And al-ghawā is the bloating of the suckling camel-calf; this was said by Yaʿqūb in al-Iṣlāḥ. It was said: it is its lacking milk until it dies of hunger; this was said by al-Farra', and al-Ṭabarī reported it. It is said from it: ghawā yaghwī.

al-Zahrāwī reported that it is the one whose milk has been cut off until it nearly perishes, or has not yet perished. Ibn al-Anbārī said: that the meaning of yughwiyakum is yuhlikakum is a view to be avoided. Makki denied that ghawā with the meaning of perdition exists in the language of the Arabs, but this is refuted by the transmission of al-Farra' and others. If the meaning of yughwiyakum is yuhlikakum, then there is no evidence in it either for a Mu'tazilite or for a Sunni; the proof lies elsewhere. Its meaning is: since you are determined in disbelief, the station in which the counsels of God, His admonitions and all His kindnesses do not benefit you, how would my counsel benefit you? [p. 220]

In His words ﴿He is your Lord﴾ there is an alert to knowledge of the Creator, and that He is the One who looks to your welfare; if He wills to lead you astray, and if He wills to guide you. And in His words ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Yunus: 56] there is a threat and a warning.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say: "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit."﴾ It was said: this verse is inserted within the story of Nuh, and the reports in it concern the Quraysh. They say that to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), i.e. he has invented the Qur'an, and invented this account about Nuh and his people. If that were established by a sound chain, it would be accepted. But the apparent meaning is that the pronoun in "they say" refers to the people of Nuh, i.e. "Or do they say he has invented what he informed them of from the religion of God and the punishment of those who turn away from it?" So he, peace be upon him, said: "Say: If I have invented it, then upon me is the sin of my crime." The word ijrām is a verbal noun of ajrama, and it is said: ajrama means "to commit much," and jarama has the same meaning.

From it is the saying of the poet:

"An outcast of his tribe, and a pledge for a sin, for what my hand has committed and my tongue has done."

It was read: (ajrāmī) with a fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of jurm, mentioned by al-Naḥḥās, and it was explained as "my sins."

The meaning of ﴿of what you commit﴾: of your crime in attributing the invention to me. It was said: "of what you commit" means of disbelief and denial.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 11, verses 36–40 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they have been doing."﴾ ﴿And make the ark under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who did wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾

The majority of readers recited (وأُوحِيَ) in the passive voice, and (أنَّهُ) with a fatha on the hamza. Abu al-Barhasam recited (وأوْحى) in the active voice, and (إنَّهُ) with a kasra on the hamza. This is according to the school of the Basrans (al-Basriyyun) by supposing an implied verb of saying (إضمار القول), and according to the school of the Kufans (al-Kufiyyun) by treating (أوحى) as (قال). The meaning is that God made Noah despair of their faith, and that it had become, by God's report about them, something as impossible as it is rationally inconceivable.

The meaning of ﴿except those who have already believed﴾ is: except those from whom what was expected of their faith has been found. God forbade him from being distressed (ابتئاس) over what they were doing, which is his grief over them in a state of humbled submission. (ابتأس) is a form of (افتعل) derived from (البؤس, misery). It is said: "ابتأس الرجل" when something he dislikes reaches him. A poet said:

*"How many a friend or intimate have I lost, yet I did not grieve, though the loss in it is great."*

Another said:

*"Whatever God distributes, accept it without being distressed, and sit down noble, with a comfortable mind."*

Another said:

*"The horseman of the horses, when the mistress of the curtain wails with a grieving voice."*

Another said:

*"In a mourning gathering like the ewes of Sara, who grieve over what has befallen us." (Sara: a place name.)*

﴿over what they have been doing﴾ — of denying you, harming you, and opposing you — for the time of retribution against them has come. (واصنع, "and make") is coordinated with ﴿so do not grieve﴾. (بأعيننا, "under Our eyes") means: in Our sight, under Our watch and protection, so that his workmanship does not deviate from the correct course, and no one comes between him and the work. The plural here is like the singular, as in God's words: ﴿and that you may be brought up under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39], but it is pluralized here to increase the watchfulness, protection and their continuity.

Talha ibn Musarrif recited (بِأعيّنا) with assimilation (مدغمة). (ووحينا, "and by Our inspiration") means: We inspire you and inspire you in how to make it. It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he did not know how to make the ark, so God inspired him to make it like the breast of a bird. It has been said that (بأعيننا) may also mean: by Our angels whom We made as eyes over the places of your protection and assistance, so that the word here is genuinely plural. As for the view of those who say that (ووحينا) means "by Our command to you" or "by Our knowledge," it is weak, because His saying ﴿and make the ark﴾ suffices without that.

In a hadith: "Jibril was the zan of Noah's ship," and the zan is the one in charge of the ship's operation.

Those who did wrong are the people of Noah. He had already been told not to intercede for them and request their respite. He gave as the reason for forbidding him to address Him that He had decreed their drowning, and forbade him from asking for its reversal, as in His saying: ﴿O Abraham, turn away from this; indeed the command of your Lord has come, and indeed a punishment that cannot be turned back is coming upon them﴾ [Hud: 76] [p. 221]. It has been said that those who did wrong were his wife Wa'ila and his son Kan'an.

﴿And he was making the ark, and every time a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said: "If you mock us, then we will mock you as you mock.﴾ ﴿So you will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment.﴾ ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven gushed forth, We said: "Load into it two of every kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already preceded, and those who believed." But none believed with him except a few.﴾

﴿And he was making the ark﴾: a narration of a past state. The ark (الفلك) is the ship. When God commanded him to make the ark, he said: "My Lord, I am not a carpenter." He said: "Yes, but this is by My eye." So he took the adze, and his hand did not miss. They would pass by him and say: "This one who claims to be a prophet has become a carpenter?" It has been said that the angels taught him, and he hired laborers who worked with him in carving. God inspired him: "Hasten the work on the ship, for My anger has intensified against those who disobeyed Me." Sam, Ham and Japheth were carving with him. The wood was of teak (الساج), as stated by Qatada, Ikrima and al-Kalbi.

It has been said that he planted it for twenty years. It has been said: three hundred years, planting, cutting and drying. Amr ibn al-Harith said: he did not plant it, but cut it from Mount Lebanon. Ibn Abbas said: it was of the wood of al-Shimshar (a type of cedar-like wood), which is al-Baqs, a piece from Mount Lebanon. They differed about its shape, whether square or long, about the duration of its making, the place where it was made, and the measurements of its length and width, in conflicting statements, none of which is authentically established.

Their mockery of him was because they saw him building a ship, and they had never seen a ship built before. They said: "O Noah, what are you making?" He said: "I am building a house that will walk upon the water." They wondered at his words and mocked him, as stated by Muqatil.

It has also been said: because he was building in a village not near the sea. They would laugh and say: "O Noah, you have become a carpenter after you were a prophet."

(وكلما) is an adverbial phrase of time, whose governing element is (سخروا منه). (قال) is a new sentence (مستأنف) according to the supposition of a questioner's question. They allowed that the governing element could be (قال). (سخروا) is a description of (ملأ) or a substitute for (مر). The substitution is unlikely, because (سخر) does not have the meaning of (مر), since the meaning of "mocking" is not intended to be "passing" or any kind of it.

Ibn Atiyya said: "They mocked him: they considered him ignorant. If the matter was as reported, that they had never seen a ship nor was there one, then the reason for considering him ignorant is clear, and the commentaries are unanimous on this. But if ships were known at that time, then they considered him ignorant regarding building it in a village not near the sea," end of quote.

﴿Indeed, we mock you﴾: in the future, as you mock us now, i.e., like your mockery when you are drowned in this world and burned in the Hereafter. Or: if you consider us ignorant regarding what we do, then we consider you ignorant regarding what you are upon of disbelief and exposing yourselves to God's wrath and punishment; you are more deserving of being called ignorant than we are. Al-Zajjaj said something close to this meaning. Or: if you consider us ignorant, then we consider you ignorant in your considering us ignorant, because you only consider someone ignorant out of ignorance of the reality of the matter and based on the outward appearance, as is the custom of the ignorant in staying far from realities. [p. 222]

Ibn Juraij said: if you mock us in this world, then we will mock you in the Hereafter. Mockery (السخرية) is considering someone ignorant together with ridicule.

In His saying ﴿you will soon know﴾ there is a severe threat. The disgracing punishment is the drowning, and the lasting punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter, because it is continuous upon them, perpetual. (مَن يأتيه) is the object of (تعلمون), and (ما) is a relative pronoun. The transitivity of (تعلمون) to one object is a usage in the common idiomatic manner of transitivity to one object.

Ibn Atiyya said: it is permissible that the transitivity be to two objects, and it was restricted to one. But it is not permissible to delete the second object by restriction, because its origin is the predicate of a subject, nor by abbreviation here, because there is no indication of its deletion, and because of their scorn in His saying: ﴿who will receive it﴾. It has been said: (مَن) is an interrogative in the position of nominative as the subject, (يأتيه) is the predicate, and the clause is in the position of accusative; (تعلمون) is suspended, and the clause takes the place of the two objects. Al-Zahrawi reported that he read (ويَحُلُّ) with a damma on the ha', and (ويَحِلُّ) with a kasra, meaning: and it is obligatory.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the descent of the religion and of the binding truth from which there is no separation, and the meaning of (يخزيه): he exposes him, or destroys him, or humiliates him, which is the drowning. These are closely related statements.

﴿Until when Our command came﴾: the discussion of the entry of (حتى) upon (إذا) was mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-An'am. Here it is a limit for His saying ﴿and he was making the ark﴾. (يصنع), as we said, is a narration of a state: i.e., he was making the ark until the time of the promised threat came.

The sentence is a transmitted state: (وكلما مر عليه) is a circumstantial clause, as if it was said: "he was making it, while the state was that whenever a company passed by him." (أمرنا) is the singular of "matters" or a verbal noun, i.e., Our command to the gushing, or to the clouds for their release, and to the angels for disposing of that, and similar things that are destined in the calamity.

(فار) means: it erupted with force. (التنور) is the face of the earth, and the Arabs call it a tannur, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyayna. Or (التنور) is the oven in which bread is baked; it was of stone, and it belonged to Hawwa' until it came to Noah, as stated by al-Hasan and Mujahid, and reported also from Ibn Abbas. It has been said: it was Adam's; it has been said: it was Noah's oven. Or: the highest part of the earth and the raised places, as stated by Qatada. Or: the spring in the island, the spring of al-Warda, reported by Ikrima. Or: from the farthest part of Noah's house, as stated by Muqatil. Or: the place where water gathers in the ship, reported from al-Hasan. Or: the rising of the sun, reported from Ali. Or: the light of dawn, from their saying "نَوَّرَ الفَجْرُ تنويرًا" (the dawn brightened), as stated by Ali and Mujahid. Or: it is a metaphor, and what is meant is the overwhelming of water and the manifestation of the punishment, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said at the intensity of battle: "The oven has grown hot" (حمي الوطيس). Al-Watis also means the place where fire is kindled, so there is no difference between (حمي) and (فار), since both are used for fire. God the Exalted said: ﴿they will hear its roaring while it boils﴾ [al-Mulk: 7]. There is no difference between (الوطيس) and (التنور). The apparent meaning of these statements is to understand it as the oven, which is the place where fire is kindled. It is possible that (ال) in it is for a specific known oven, and it is possible that it is generic, so that the fire erupted from the ovens, and that was among the most wondrous things, that water should boil from the place where fires are kindled.

There is no contradiction between this and His saying ﴿and We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], since it is possible that by "the earth" is meant the places of the ovens. The gushing (التفجير) is different from the boiling (الفوران), so the boiling was for the oven and the gushing was for the earth.

The pronoun in (فيها) refers to the ark, which is masculine but was made feminine according to the meaning of ship (السفينة), and likewise His saying ﴿and he said: "Board it"﴾ [Hud: 41].

Hafs recited ﴿of every kind two pairs﴾ with tanwin on (كل), meaning: of every animal; (زوجين) is the object, and (اثنين) is an emphatic adjective. The rest of the seven readers recited it with the genitive construction, and (اثنين) is the object of (احمل). (زوجين) is in the general sense, meaning: of everything that has a mate. This is the meaning of "of every kind two pairs," as stated by Abu Ali and others.

Ibn Atiyya said: if the meaning were: "load in it two of every pair, each of which is two loaders," it would be obligatory that he carry four of every kind. The word (زوج) in the well-known usage of the Arabs means one of a pair that has a mate, so it is said: "this is the mate of this," and "they are two mates," and this is the established usage in the Qur'an in His saying ﴿eight pairs﴾ [al-An'am: 143], then He explained them, and in His saying ﴿and that He created the pairs, the male and the female﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. Al-Akhfash said: it is sometimes said in Arabic usage for two: "zawj" (a pair). Thus the arithmetic scholars take it.

Also in Arabic usage, (زوج) means "kind," as in His saying: [p. 223] ﴿and We caused to grow in it every beautiful kind﴾ [Qaf: 7], and His saying: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the kinds﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36], end of quote.

When the rain began to fall like the mouths of waterskins, the wild animals began seeking the middle of the earth fleeing from the water, until they gathered near the ark. God commanded him to carry two of each pair, meaning a male and a female, so that the root of the offspring would remain after the Flood. It is reported that the animal kinds would come to him, and he would place his right hand on the male and his left on the female. The ark had three levels: the lowest for the wild animals, the middle for food and drink, and the upper for him and those who believed.

(وأهلك) is coordinated with (زوجين) if (كل) is with tanwin, and with (اثنين) if it is in the genitive construction. He excepted from his family whoever the word of destruction had preceded regarding, and that he was among the people of the Fire.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "The word preceded regarding him that he would choose disbelief, not because of God's decree upon him and His will to other than that," end of quote.

This is on the path of the Mu'tazila (i'tizal). The one against whom the word preceded was his wife Wa'ila, with an unpointed ʿayn, and his son Kan'an.

﴿And those who believed﴾: coordinated with (وأهلك). It has been said that they were eighty men and eighty women. It has been said that they were seventy-three.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Eighty men believed with him." And from him: "Eighty people": three of his sons, Sam, Ham and Yafith, and three of his daughters-in-law (kanāʾin).

When they came out of the ship, they built a town called today "the Town of the Eighty" in the region of Mosul.

It was also said: they were seventy-eight, half of them men and half of them women.

Ibn Ishaq said: they were ten, besides their wives: Nuh, and his sons Sam, Ham and Yafith, and six men from among those who had believed in him, and their wives, all of them. And from Ibn Ishaq: they were ten: five men and five women.

It was said: they were nine: Nuh and eight sons of his, and his wife. It was also said: they were eight, and Nuh and his wife, other than the one who was punished, and his three sons and their wives. This is the saying of Qatadah, al-Hakam, Ibn ʿUyaynah, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb.

Al-Aʿmash said: they were seven: Nuh, three daughters-in-law (kanāʾin), and three sons. These are conflicting sayings. What Allah, exalted is He, has informed us of is that only a few believed with him, and the number of this small group, whose number Allah has left unspecified, cannot be determined with certainty except by an explicit text from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 11, verses 36–40 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they have been doing."﴾ ﴿And make the ark under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who did wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾

The meaning is that God made Noah despair of their faith, and that it had become, by God's report about them, something as impossible as it is rationally inconceivable.

The meaning of ﴿except those who have already believed﴾ is: except those from whom what was expected of their faith has been found. God forbade him from being distressed (ابتئاس) over what they were doing, which is his grief over them in a state of humbled submission. (ابتأس) is a form of (افتعل) derived from (البؤس, misery). It is said: "ابتأس الرجل" when something he dislikes reaches him. A poet said:

*"How many a friend or intimate have I lost, yet I did not grieve, though the loss in it is great."*

Another said:

*"Whatever God distributes, accept it without being distressed, and sit down noble, with a comfortable mind."*

Another said:

*"The horseman of the horses, when the mistress of the curtain wails with a grieving voice."*

Another said:

﴿over what they have been doing﴾ — of denying you, harming you, and opposing you — for the time of retribution against them has come. (واصنع, "and make") is coordinated with ﴿so do not grieve﴾. It was also said: they were seventy-eight, half of them men and half of them women.
